sources.title: Peru Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical indicators through 2019; climate and development projections to 2050 and 2100
sources.methodology: World Bank synthesis of climate, socioeconomic and institutional diagnostics with referenced quantitative estimates.
sources.limitations: Dated 2022 with mixed indicator vintages; a national development report, not a conflict study, and attribution varies by estimate.

sources.title: Peru: Strategic Actions Toward Water Security
sources.temporal_coverage: Diagnostic studies conducted 2019–2021; model projections for 2030 and 2050
sources.methodology: Water-security diagnostic using local hydrological data, satellite evapotranspiration, demand databases and SENAMHI climate projections.
sources.limitations: Mixed study vintages and model assumptions; basin deficits are not 2026 measurements, and conflict discussion does not establish climate attribution.

sources.title: Plan Multisectorial ante Lluvias Intensas y Peligros Asociados 2025–2027
sources.organization: Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros (PCM), with CENEPRED
geographic_coverage: Peru; district risk scenarios and multisector interventions
sources.temporal_coverage: Plan period 2025–2027; susceptibility analysis draws on historical El Niño/La Niña episodes and records through April 2024
sources.methodology: Government risk plan combines hazard susceptibility, district exposure and vulnerability with agency intervention targets.
sources.limitations: ENSO-based risk scenario is not an event forecast or anthropogenic attribution; intervention targets are not verified delivery outcomes.

sources.title: Informe N.º 12-2025-OGASA: Conflictos socioambientales, diciembre 2025
sources.organization: Ministerio del Ambiente (MINAM), Oficina General de Asuntos Socio-Ambientales (OGASA)
geographic_coverage: Peru; named socio-environmental cases in Puno and other regions
sources.temporal_coverage: December 2025 monthly monitoring; annual alert totals through December 2025
sources.methodology: Official monthly administrative monitoring of socio-environmental cases, alerts and agency commitments.
sources.limitations: Agency case and commitment records are not independent verification, climate attribution or impact evaluation.

sources.title: Follow the Water: Emerging Issues of Climate Change and Conflict in Peru
sources.organization: Foundation for Environmental Security and Sustainability (FESS), prepared for USAID Office of Conflict Management and Mitigation
geographic_coverage: Santa River Basin and Huaraz, Ancash
sources.methodology: Original field interviews in Lima, Huaraz/Santa River Basin and highland Arequipa.
sources.limitations: 2012 discussion paper expressly not official USAID; qualitative interviews, no causal evaluation.

claims.locator: Printed p. 8, section 1.1.1, ‘Geography, climate, and socioeconomics.’
claims.paraphrase: The report associates El Niño with more flooding on the Costa and drought in the Sierra; agriculture and fisheries’ large employment and export shares add exposure.
claims.limitations: Reported El Niño association, not event-by-event anthropogenic attribution.

claims.paraphrase: The report says informality, inequality and low safe-water/sanitation access increase climate welfare vulnerability; 73% of employed people had informal jobs in 2019, with worker poverty rates over four times formal peers.
claims.limitations: Employment figure is national and dated 2019; it is not a locality-specific climate impact estimate.

claims.paraphrase: The report describes weak national–regional coordination and limited subnational DRM participation; only 13 regions, 28 provinces and 39 districts had prevention plans, while central authorities led the 2017 El Niño emergency outside the DRM framework.
geographies: Peru; regional, provincial and district levels
claims.limitations: The report is dated 2022; plan counts and 2017 response describe its cited period, not current institutional status.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 24–25, Box 4.1, water-balance assessment and Map B4.1.1.
claims.paraphrase: The diagnostic’s approximately 5-km water-balance model found deficits in 72 of 231 basins; six additional basins could enter deficit under its RCP8.5 projection.
claims.scenario: The report labels the additional-basin map RCP8.5 for 2030 and describes broader model projections for 2030 and 2050.
claims.limitations: The baseline and modeled scenario are diagnostic estimates, not 2026 basin measurements.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 24 and 26, Rimac Basin and northern-coast water-stress discussion.
claims.paraphrase: The report identifies the Rimac Basin as the sharpest deficit: Lima’s 11 million residents rely on Atlantic-region transfers for several months yearly; north-coast irrigated agriculture is also threatened by scarcity.
claims.limitations: Diagnostic description; not household-level access data or a 2026 measurement.

claims.locator: Printed p. 11, irrigation coverage and regional poverty discussion.
claims.paraphrase: In Sierra and Alta Selva, where half of rural residents are poor, only about 20% of cultivated land is irrigated, leaving farming exposed to rainfall shifts; most Costa agricultural land is irrigated.
claims.limitations: The poverty and irrigation figures have different denominators; underlying data vintages vary.

claims.locator: Printed p. 25 and Annex 4, flood-risk scenario and very-high-risk district list.
claims.paraphrase: Under possible summer El Niño/La Niña rainfall anomalies, the plan rates 78 districts across 12 departments very high flood risk, covering 2.396 million people; Annex 4 names Belén and Piura districts including Catacaos and Tambogrande.
claims.scenario: Potential January–March rainfall anomalies associated with historical El Niño and La Niña episodes; a risk scenario, not a dated event forecast or climate-change projection.
claims.limitations: Modeled risk exposure; population counts do not imply observed damage or event-specific losses.

claims.locator: Printed p. 71, Intervention Sheet 31, community early-warning systems.
claims.paraphrase: For 2025–2027, the plan assigns INDECI technical assistance to reactivate or optimize 43 community early-warning systems and strengthen 122 others for intense-rain hazards.
claims.scenario: Plan target for 2025–2027; the document states an intended intervention, not achieved coverage.
geographies: Peru; priority high- and very-high-risk areas
claims.limitations: The 43/122 figures are planned targets, not verified activation or performance results.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 1–2, executive summary, December 2025 case and commitment totals.
claims.paraphrase: MINAM prioritized 39 cases, OEFA 23 and SERNANP 14; MINAM reported 342 of 379 commitments across 35 cases complete, 25 in process, 12 pending, and 100 alerts issued during 2025.
claims.limitations: Commitment completion denominator is 379 commitments, not 39 cases; agency status is not an outcome evaluation.

claims.locator: Printed p. 9, Alert Report 095-2025-OGASA-MINAM, dated 11 December 2025.
claims.paraphrase: Authorities and residents of Ocuviri and Vila Vila, Puno, demanded environmental remediation of the Hatun Ayllu basin and a plenary session involving ministers and other senior officials.
claims.limitations: An official alert summary of demands; it does not establish contamination findings or climate attribution.

claims.locator: Printed p. 26, case 29, Llallimayo basin status through 18 December 2025.
claims.paraphrase: The Llallimayo case covers Ayaviri, Cupi, Llalli and Umachiri in Melgar, Puno; an environmental-recovery worktable expired in December 2025 after a 2020 rights action was suspended, and local actors sought a replacement development table.
institutions: Frente de Defensa de los Recursos Hídricos de la Cuenca Llallimayo
claims.limitations: Status and requests are agency-reported as of December 2025; no climate link is stated.

claims.locator: Printed p. 40, Santa River Basin field findings, Huaraz and surrounding areas.
claims.paraphrase: Huascarán Park’s head said glacier retreat, warming and erratic rain were weakening Cordillera Blanca wetlands’ and pastures’ water regulation; low-income settlers and illegal miners were entering sensitive highlands exposed to glacial-lake outbursts.
claims.limitations: 2012 interview attributed to the Park head; not an independent causal assessment.

claims.locator: Printed p. 34, ‘Harmonizing Economic Development and Environmental Protection,’ MINAM interview account.
claims.paraphrase: An interviewed MINAM director said warming-related crop and herder shifts may intensify Andean resource competition.
claims.limitations: Interview hypothesis, not measured competition or violence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The official linked climate-related livelihood shifts to potential Andean resource competition.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 42–43, Canrey Chico community account, Recuay, Ancash.
claims.paraphrase: Canrey Chico leaders said two decades of learning, a water group and improved farming raised pasture quality and reduced conflict; they reported declining a mining proposal.
affected_groups: Canrey Chico community leaders and residents
claims.limitations: Participant account, not evaluation; no climate-causation claim.

search_audit.query: Peru climate change subnational vulnerability Andes Amazon drought flooding Indigenous regions official World Bank CCDR climate report
search_audit.outcome: Opened full CCDR, Water Security Diagnostic and government flood-risk plan; extracted named basin, region and district examples while separating historical hazards from modeled risk.

search_audit.query: Peru climate conflict water scarcity mining Indigenous communities climate security conflict official report
search_audit.outcome: The 2012 field report records a qualified potential climate–resource-competition mechanism; 2023 water and 2025 official conflict records document water/mining grievances without climate attribution. No contemporary tested climate-to-violence finding was located.

search_audit.query: Peru conflict violence insecurity impacts climate adaptation environmental institutions Indigenous territories official report
search_audit.outcome: Reviewed local case management, subnational DRM and field-research passages; the inspected sources document capacity and coordination constraints but do not establish current insecurity as a constraint on climate-adaptation delivery.

search_audit.query: Peru local climate adaptation resilience glaciers drought communities regional plan official government UN
search_audit.outcome: Opened the 2025–2027 multisector plan and reviewed water-management and community accounts; early-warning and local-capacity evidence is either a stated plan target or qualitative historical testimony, not verified current outcomes.

gaps: Recent official conflict monitoring gives named cases in Puno and other departments but does not attribute these cases to climate hazards.

The only inspected source explicitly discussing climate-related conflict mechanisms is a 2012 nonofficial, qualitative field discussion paper; its competition pathway is an attributed potential mechanism, not a tested causal finding or proof of violence.

No reverse pathway from current insecurity or conflict to climate-adaptation implementation was established in the inspected evidence; the CCDR's subnational DRM constraints are not attributed to FCV.
The 2025–2027 government plan records intended targets, not verified delivery; national and basin diagnostics cannot substitute for current site-level implementation evidence.
